column8: Thu 19 Nov: store; a mortgage as a dead pledge is a true frame for the first plan's one date (8s: a shortfall on 1 Jan 2033 with no money after January 2028), but 3f names no outside source (panel 4) and 3a has Antonio; never one of ten dates.
Thu 19 Nov: store; leases wrote their grace in advance, a lineage fact behind Table 3's dated lines that decides nothing; section numbers unconfirmed.
Thu 19 Nov: store, the evidence behind row 25's reading of IPS l.13 (late, whole, before anyone relies on it); Spence read only as the Supreme Court quotes him.

Thu 19 Nov: store; equity turning open-ended forgiveness into a named short day is the lineage of Table 3 dating IPS l.17's two words (definitions, never new triggers, CANON A34); row 15 gives the reason, so use that one.
Thu 19 Nov: store; Blackstone's ground for relief (cover in value, a date missed) annotates Antonio's nine-times cover (Q163-004), not Laura, whose ten secure no lender.
Thu 19 Nov: store; Shylock's according to the tenour was the common law of Shakespeare's day (Makdessi para 4), context for Q163-004 to -006 in 3a, never named in 3f (panel 4).

Thu 19 Nov: store; the law's definition of whole for a late payment (the sum, interest for the wait, costs), which Q138-015's zero-interest standard already prices at nothing for her; the statute itself unread.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q163-004: the same bond in 1.3, its form beside its cover; one row for the bond is enough.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a store, the fuller reading of Q163-006: Bassanio tenders twice the sum, Portia thrice, Shylock wants the tenour, the step the 1705 Act later made a defence; the tendered money was Portia's; 3a only, never 3f (the card's best-three item 3 breaks panel 4's no outside name in 3f).
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q176-011: Peachy's test (relief where money alone was wanted, none where nothing can compensate) is idea 1 in older, harder words; row 11 says it plainly.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a, one clause on why each payment's date is bought, not only its sum: money at a date when receipt had lost its usefulness is the residency's January in the law's words (8u: late on its 1 January is broken); quote it as Lord Wilberforce's account of Eldon (Hill v Barclay unread); deepens Q163-006; a partner for Antonio, never a second name in 3a.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q176-011: the same judgment and relation (no buying one's way out by a later, unpromised payment).
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q176-011: Makdessi para 10 is idea 1's modern statement (late compliance plus compensation); one row carries it.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a store, or one clause with row 11: ten minutes late cost a buyer the flat and HK$420,000, the law's own picture of a payee for whom the date is the bargain, as the residency's 1 January is; keep Kowalski's critique (the vendor gained and never showed the 5 pm mattered).

Thu 19 Nov: 3e or Table 3's note, store: Hoffmann's reason that an undefined discretion breeds uncertainty is why Table 3 dates IPS l.17's two words (31 March 2028; five business days), definitions never triggers (CANON A34, Q34-029); for Laura the risk is her own team re-arguing a reason under stress.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q176-014: read only as Union Eagle cites it; the same relation, a working asset's owner needs the date.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e store, the evidence behind row 24: open-ended grace grieves whoever relies on the date, which is why Table 3 row 5 lets a trade slip day by day but never past the 2031 meetings; Eldon read only through Kent.
Thu 19 Nov: store; one railroad's six months is lineage for row 27's list and serves no part.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q53-033: the law guards a principal date hardest (interest has grace, principal none); TIA s.316 adds a source, and Treasuries sit outside the Act.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q138-012: a Treasury states no grace period, so the five-day line is borrowed (Q8b-028); Russia's 30 days is only the contrast.

Thu 19 Nov: store, 3e one clause at most: Russia paid inside its grace but left out about $1.9 million of interest for the wait and a failure to pay was ruled, the 1705 rule in 2022; for Laura Q138-015 already prices a delay at nothing.
Thu 19 Nov: store; a currency switch cannot happen to a Treasury paying in its own currency, so contrast only.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the market counts the holder's receipt, so paid has a custody side (SKELETON item 4 (c); Q2b-026's 1985 plumbing case); a sanctions block, never a risk named for her Treasuries.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e or Table 3's note, the card's strongest and checkable: every grace the plan allows ends before anyone relies on the money (deposit by 31 March 2028, trades never past the 2031 meetings, five business days falling 7-9 days before a fund-paid 1 January, the residency's 1 January none), checked against Table 3 and 8u; the general form of Q53-033 and of Q165-024's fix; Keel synthesis.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 2.2 store: IPS l.13's completion read as an equity of redemption, late (January 2028), whole (the $2,388 top-up, NUMBERS 0) and five years before the first payment; the completion is the top-up only, never the extra Treasuries (WORDS); a frame beside Q163-029, never in Laura's words.

Thu 19 Nov: the correction, kept as the parent's guard: the first plan's misses were value short on its one date (97.5% had shares lower after 2027-2030, NUMBERS 8s, checked), not late money, so Q163-004, Q163-005, Q163's idea 2 and the AHA register's Antonio candidate need the fix: Antonio in 3a for why a date is bought, never solvent but late for the first plan.

Thu 19 Nov: store; fix: drop as money moved faster (no source shows the cause) and Union Eagle (a contract term, not a grace norm); keep it a list of grace lengths behind why five business days sits at the short end.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q8b-028, whose note and Q138-012's already say the five-day line is the report's definition (Keel's call, Wed 11 Nov), never the IPS's.

Thu 19 Nov: store; Franklin dropped a fixed 2,000 pounds for a canal years away and let interest grow his gift instead, while the case lets co-sponsors pay the rest (l.83-86) so Laura's part can be owned; Franklin had no co-funders waiting.
Thu 19 Nov: store; a word-level contrast (a state's IOUs sold for the gift) that serves no part.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a, the card's aha and a new relation: Franklin's 131,000 pounds needed every repaid pound lent again at 5%, the reinvestment bet the ten are sized against (paid even if cash waiting earns nothing, NUMBERS 2), one sentence beside the extra Treasuries; the rungs still reinvest (WN l.18) but do not depend on it; competes with Antonio for 3a's one outside name.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q167-006: 1.05 to the 100th is compound-interest lore; the projection is already there.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c, one clause, or CONCEIT as a true fact behind the working word pencil: the patron saint of compound interest called his own projection a possible vain fancy; never a new turn; honesty by wording suits a hope nobody plans around, and co-sponsors plan around hers (case l.114).
Thu 19 Nov: store; Franklin trusted later managers and his fund needed seven rulings, while IPS l.17 writes its exits now; keep the two reasons and the ways a promise fails as two lists (Q109).

Thu 19 Nov: store, the base for every Franklin percentage: about three-fifths on Vierling's base (4.8666 dollars a pound), about two-thirds only at the 1791 rate (4.44); corrects Q166-028's about two-thirds and confirms Q167-007's fix: say well short or about three-fifths, never two percentages without a base.
Thu 19 Nov: store; half a point a year for a century took off two-fifths (Keel arithmetic, checked), pedigree on compounding; after the move her top has no rate in it.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q179-003 as its evidence: the craftsmen stopped borrowing after 1886 (the court's reasons, Vierling's line), the engine Q166-028 and Q167-007 already name.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e or 3a store: Franklin named two ways his money could fail, lie dead or be diverted, and both happened; the standard answers the first and l.17's no other reason the second, kept apart from the list of ways a promise fails (Q109); Philadelphia's diversion rests on one magazine history.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q167-005: the heirs' delay, now to the school's opening in 1908; the delays were legal, not financial; the division figures conflict.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q166-028 (Philadelphia about a fifth): every Philadelphia figure differs by source and none is primary.

Thu 19 Nov: store; fix the use: half the shares stay promised to no one for IPS l.15's three uses in its own order, never because the building's need is not set; Franklin's hedge on the use is colour.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c, one clause, the sharper form of Q167-007: a banker's 1923 forecast from the fund's own century still overshot the 1991 result by about half (7.15 million against 4.65 million dollars), so nothing is stated before the move; NUMBERS 4's 10.6%, 8.6%, 6.2% and 2.9% (12, 6, 3, 1 months) checked; say the move would buy less than a top stated early; competes with the Opera House Act for 3c's one name.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q179-014: two rates are not a range, as the card says; NUMBERS 4's $95,000 / $115,000 / $140,000 checked.
Thu 19 Nov: store; on the day Franklin's 200-year figure fell due, three-quarters of it was loans receivable (Keel arithmetic, checked), a timing point for certainty has dates, not a loss.

Thu 19 Nov: 3c store; fix: the $4,772 is Keel arithmetic ($122,503 less $117,731) not in NUMBERS, so book it with the numbers owner or quote NUMBERS 3's 2.32% and 6.12% of what the late-2032 fund pays on its two purchases; never the two funds.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q179-003: the plan side of the same relation, every figure already in NUMBERS 2 and the store (Q64-013, Q64-034); 325 of 585 checked (39 plus 286); never usually small or a bare 55.6%.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q152-040: the early end's $4,589 and 1.92% (NUMBERS 3) checked; the Franklin frame adds nothing to Table 3 row 4.

Thu 19 Nov: 3d, one clause behind her figure is their target (SD-1): Carnegie's letter offered to duplicate the fund to the cent, $408,396.48, the figure that existed, never Franklin's projection; what survives of Q167's lead; quote duplicate as his word, never match for co-sponsors (WORDS); competes with Nicaea for 3d's one name.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q179-020: the same letter's sequel; Carnegie may simply have kept to his letter, one case.
Thu 19 Nov: store; a corporate bond called at 115 is textbook call risk, and Laura's Treasuries cannot be called; Table 3 row 4 has closer precedents (Q3c-007, Q151 rows).

Thu 19 Nov: store, the correction: Carnegie's bonds earned about a ninth of the school's 1921-22 income (Keel arithmetic, checked), so Q167-008's use (a co-funder's bonds for the running money) and Q167-009's lead aha (owned running money lasted) are overturned, with Q167's idea 2 (a second giver supplied the running money), its best-three item 1 and SKELETON 3.0's challenger 2; say about a ninth, never that Carnegie paid none.

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 or 3a store: in 1956 the school borrowed to meet its payroll because a court held Carnegie's principal could not pay it, so a building with capital owned and running money left to fees ran short; overturns Q167-009; the case lets program fees fund running costs beyond her ten, never the ten (l.84-86, l.91-92).
Thu 19 Nov: store; one more overrun beside card Q172's, with two conflicting cost figures (Q167-008's $402,718 is one of them); facility costs are outside the case (l.164).

Thu 19 Nov: store; Smithson's money was lost once in Arkansas and Michigan bonds, a named victim of the 1841-42 state defaults (H5-049 holds the relation: Treasuries only is itself a safety rule); the 1842 detail conflicts.

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 or 3b, one sentence with row 28: the 1846 Act lent Smithson's money to the US Treasury and built only from interest already earned; never call her reserve an endowment (it spends principal on ten dates and ends in 2042).

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 store: the Regents finished the building only once its upkeep money was saved, Laura's order (running money first), and the rescue was Congress's honour, the other people's money IPS l.11 gives up; read in an excerpt of the report page.
Thu 19 Nov: store, writers' note only: vain fancy against Trading Note 3's vain illusion is a word echo, colour by Q167's rule; 3f names no outside source and it is never a conceit turn.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b (Athens ranks first for its one name) or 3e, the card's strongest: 2.24 set the thousand talents aside and in the same sentence paid the war from the other money, as IPS l.15 names her flexibility in the paragraph that states the range; sharpens Q166-007 and -008; her flexibility is her own, about $21,200 (8o).

Thu 19 Nov: 3e store: the death penalty bound only the proposer and the chair, so the rule guarded the agenda, and Laura is proposer, chair and voter at once, so the payments rest on Treasuries paying on their dates, not on l.17 holding in a panic; companion Q186-013 (irrevocable, no).
Thu 19 Nov: store; the idle-ship reserve may have lapsed (a scholar's possible), a contrast with Treasuries that earn while they wait (8n).
Thu 19 Nov: store; Athens's two-vote procedure (immunity first, then spending), the mechanism 8.15 ran in one panic; it explains the parallel, not the plan.
Thu 19 Nov: store, idea 3's break: Athens guarded its citizens' tax like Athena's money, while co-sponsors are the building's first resort and ruled out for the payments (IPS l.11).
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q184-001 as its ledger: tribute, loans and a debt to the gods were the other money that took every shock for nineteen years.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q184-020 as evidence of the fourth lever (the 425 figure is a target, not a receipt).
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q184-020 as evidence (the 428 tax and the 413 levy, through Blamire; Thucydides' wording unread).
Thu 19 Nov: store; adds Athens to Q166-001's thing-paid lever (a payer that wrote its own rate cut it to 1.2%); her Treasuries' terms are fixed when bought.

Thu 19 Nov: store; in 413 Thucydides counted no money in the treasury while the thousand talents sat untouched, so guarded money was not counted as money (mental accounting, H4-120); the payments' Treasuries are never counted as building money.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b with row 1, sharpening Q166-008: the rule fell when the greatest ally revolted and the rest might follow, the co-sponsor-falling-short use in IPS l.15; Chios gave ships, not grants, and l.15's three uses are ranked by no one (WORDS).

Thu 19 Nov: the correction for Q166-008's break and the AHA register's Athens candidate: Athens did not stretch the exit, it lifted the penalty openly because 2.24's condition (a fleet attacking the city) was not met, and spent on a fleet for Ionia; say a lawful, public repeal, never half a reading of the rule.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q166-008: the money was there in 412 after nineteen untouched years, the parent's fact; Blamire adds only a scholar's confirmation.

Thu 19 Nov: 3.0 or 3e, travelling with Athens so no second name: the reserve went to the first danger in 412, and when its own threatened in 411 the money was gone, while a Treasury bought for 2041 waits for 2041; the same relation as Q166-009 (purpose against dates) with a date on each side; say the attack threatened, never that it came.
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q184-014 as its evidence (close to exhaustion by mid-411, empty in 410, some 350T by 409/8).
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q184-014 as its break: Sparta's slowness, not the reserve, saved Athens in 411.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the scholars' quarrel (the repeal or Sicily) is the plan's question in small, but Kallet's pages are unread.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e or 3b store, Athens's order (a venture costing more than set aside, then a contributor leaving, then the rule falling); fix: NUMBERS 8q tests building costs and the Taiwan dollar together (a 1-in-20 two-year rise of 28.0% leaves her flexibility plus anything above the top $3,509 short centrally), not a share slump then a cost burst, so cite 8f for share falls; Sicily was chosen, an overrun is not.

Thu 19 Nov: merged into NUM-011, whose figures are old: 8f now gives the half kept a median of about $15,200 if shares fell over 2031-2033 against $23,000, about $12,800 after a fall of more than a fifth and $5,700 from September 1929 (checked); co-sponsors can cut in the same downturn, never fall together; the Athens mapping is Keel's.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e's lead, the fixed form of Q166-001 (whose rater asked for this fourth lever): Athens pulled more money from others first and the rule last; the payments lose all four levers (Treasuries, l.11, l.17) and the building keeps its date, scope and other funders plus her flexibility; fix: never the building keeps all four (it has no rule lever), never the date cannot move (NUMBERS 3); one synthesis row in 3e, Q166-001 or this, never both.

Thu 19 Nov: store; fix: before 2031 the plan has more than two grades (the half to be moved is earmarked but pencil until the move; the extra Treasuries come back to her), so say nothing is stated before it is owned, never two grades only; Keel's reading of Blamire.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e precision, refining Q166-007's use (the same design): 2.24 named when to spend and l.17 names when the plan would change, so they share the shape, not the job; Laura's reserve is never spent on a danger, only on its dates; the two lists stay apart (Q109).
Thu 19 Nov: store, idea 4's primary source: in 349/8 Athens guarded the festival fund against the army, the opposite pot; one outside name per part, so never beside Athens's reserve (panel 4).
Thu 19 Nov: merged into Q184-023: the same episode through Hansen; its use (nobody stands outside her own choice) is Q184-002's.
Thu 19 Nov: store; Libanius's law is disputed and unread, so never in the report until Libanius and Harris (2006) are read.
Thu 19 Nov: store; both Athenian guards fell to the whole Assembly, so a rule holds against one proposer, not a frightened crowd; Philochorus read only through Hansen.

Thu 19 Nov: store; the judge's question (why keep running money untouchable when the building needs money) is answered by the case itself (high certainty for the ten, CASE_MAP A9), so it decides nothing of Caplet's; Q77 holds the building that never happens.
